card.name: The word be after may
card.fires_on: The word "be" right after "may" in overdose or adverse-event passages, as in "may be required" or "may be seen". It also fires weakly on a few other linking words such as "of" and "is".

modes.label: may be + passive
modes.description: The word "be" after "may" and before a passive participle such as required or seen.
modes.example: Exchange transfusion or dialysis may<< be>> required as means of reversing hypotension

modes.label: Other linking words
modes.description: Occasional hits on "of" or "is" within the same kind of clinical sentence.
modes.example: may be involved. It is important to note that early manifestations of hypersensitivity, such as fever or lymphadenopathy, may be present even though rash<< is>> not evident.

card.writes: The promoted tokens are mostly non-English word starts (Russian adjective stems), so there is no clear link to the English text here.
card.plain: It fires on the word "be" in phrases like "may be seen" or "may be required" in overdose and warning text.
